subject: Re: DPA clarifications — data handling, subprocessors, breach notice (Horizon Medical)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@horizonmedical.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@horizonmedical.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — DPA clarifications (Horizon Medical)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups for your legal/compliance team so we can get the DPA questions resolved and move forward: 

Recap
- What we discussed: production inference for protected health data (PHI-adjacent use cases), need for EU/US residency options, retention controls for logs and prompt data, and breach-notification SLAs.
- Redwood role: we serve inference and manage ephemeral storage of request/response material; customers control prompts, model choices, and retention policies.

Action items / questions for Horizon legal:
1) Data roles: confirm whether Horizon will treat Redwood as a Processor and Horizon as Controller (this is our standard model).
2) Subprocessors: please confirm any internal requirements for subprocessors (e.g., only specific cloud providers allowed). I can share our current subprocessors list.
3) Breach notice: need to confirm your expectation for notification SLA (we typically commit to notifying customers as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of an incident).
4) Retention: what are your retention requirements for request logs and model prompts? Our default is 30 days for non-retained logs; we offer configurable retention to 0/7/30/90/365+ days depending on contract.

Attachments I’ll send separately: short DPA overview + current subprocessors CSV (for legal to review). Can you please confirm the best contact on your legal/compliance team (cc’ing them is fine)?

Next steps
- If your legal wants to redline, send that to me and I’ll loop in Marissa and Rishi on the commercial/legal side.
- If Horizon needs on-prem or Private deployment to meet residency controls, we can scope that as a follow-up (separate SOW).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick legal-to-legal call if that helps.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Overview.pdf (see follow-up email)

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@horizonmedical.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@horizonmedical.com>, legal@horizonmedical.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — DPA clarifications (Horizon Medical)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Our legal team (cc’d) flagged a couple of specific asks so they can triage quickly: 

1) Please confirm Redwood’s default data controller/processor language (we prefer explicit text that states Horizon is Controller, Redwood is Processor).
2) Can you provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and indicate which process personal data vs. operational telemetry? We need the list to run through our vendor intake.
3) Breach notice: Horizon requires initial notification within 48 hours of detection if personal data is involved; is that feasible? If not, what flexibility do you have?
4) Do you support EU data residency (data in EU-only infra) and can that be included in the DPA?
5) Retention: our baseline ask is retention controls so that Horizon can set prompt/log retention to 0–90 days.

Can you attach the DPA + subprocessors CSV to your reply and indicate whether Redwood performs any automated backup retention outside of the retention window (we need confirmation backups are not kept longer than stated). Also please indicate whether Redwood encrypts data at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments.

If useful, we can do a quick 30-min legal sync tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lee
Head of Data Privacy | Horizon Medical
sara.lee@horizonmedical.com

> [see above]

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — DPA clarifications (Horizon Medical)

Sara —

Appreciate the specifics. I’ve attached the DPA overview and the current subprocessors export for your intake team. Below are short answers to your numbered points: 

1) Roles: Redwood’s standard language states the customer (Horizon) is Controller and Redwood is Processor. We’ll include the explicit clause in the DPA overview attached.

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV (Redwood_Subprocessors.csv). High-level: primary cloud infra providers (AWS us-east-1, GCP us-central1), monitoring/observability providers (Datadog), error-tracking (Sentry), and a managed key provider for Private deployments. In the CSV we label whether each subprocessor may access personal data vs. operational telemetry.

3) Breach notice: our standard commitment is to notify customers as soon as reasonably possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware. We can escalate to 48 hours for customers with specific compliance needs as a contract term — that typically requires a limited SLA/contract amendment. If 48 hours is a hard requirement, we can flag that in the deal (DEAL-9876) and route to legal for an exception.

4) EU residency: yes — we support EU-only deployments (Redwood Private or dedicated EU-hosted instances). We can add an explicit EU-residency clause to the DPA for Horizon and scope it in the SOW if accepted.

5) Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention: 0 / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365+ days. Backups: we do not retain customer request/response data outside of configured retention windows in hosted flows; Private/on-prem options can mirror customer key-management and retention policies.

6) Encryption / KMS: For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For hosted accounts we use provider-managed KMS but can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for Dedicated/Enterprise plans.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_DPA_Overview.pdf (summary with standard clauses and options)
- Redwood_Subprocessors.csv (vendor list; column indicates "personal data access" = yes/no)

Next steps: 
- If Horizon wants 48-hour breach notice as standard, please confirm and we’ll create a redline request to legal.
- If your legal has redlines on controller/processor language, send them to me and I’ll loop in Marissa + Rishi for review.

Happy to do a 30-min legal-to-legal call tomorrow.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Overview.pdf; Redwood_Subprocessors.csv

Ben
